main_body: Flat brick/paving ground patch covering the whole 4x3 tile area, with a few blue-grey and light-grey inset strips. It is not a standing object.
top_band: none. The column scan crosses repeating brick courses (cream, pink-grey, dark mortar), not a top band over a front face.
evidence: The kind is terrain: a seamless ground surface with no standing volume, so the top-plus-front 3/4 contract does not apply. There is no isometric side face. The brick courses read as a ground texture. Terrain is not penalised for lacking a top band.

style.evidence: The candidate has 5 lightness steps on its brick ramp: cream 187, pink-grey 178, taupe 145, dark mortar 86 and an extra blue-grey 99. That matches the paving reference, which also has about 5 steps. Its mortar lines are neutral grey, about 30% near-neutral dark edge pixels, so the outline is mixed and not a uniform black sticker line. The 5x5 flat-fill coverage is 0%, and the bricks carry pink and cream speckle. Median colours per tile is 7 (paving reference 7, grass reference 26), and the candidate has 11 distinct colours (paving reference 7, grass reference 80). It equals the paving reference but is far below the grass reference. Since the paving reference is the same kind and is equally simple, a careful artist would accept it beside that reference.
